subject: Renewal: Dedicated capacity uplift & scaling headroom request
messages:
From: Simon Lee <simon.lee@acme-corp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nancy Ortiz <nancy.ortiz@acme-corp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Nov 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity uplift request ahead of renewal (dec)

Jonas / Marissa —

Thanks again for the hosted review last week. As we head into our December renewal, the product team is asking for firm commitments around dedicated capacity so we can finalize our internal budget and support plan. High level ask:

- Add 24 additional A100-equivalent GPUs to our Dedicated pool (bringing our reserved pool to 56 GPUs).
- A guaranteed baseline throughput target of 2200 tokens/sec (aggregate) for our primary inference route during business hours (PST).
- A scaling headroom buffer that keeps 6 GPUs "warmbuffered" for burst traffic (we call it warmbuffer internally) to avoid cold-start latency for short spikes.
- Min/max replica guidance: want a guaranteed minimum equivalent of 30 GPUs and the ability to burst to 70 with documented scale-up lag expectations.

Attached is a short spreadsheet with our projected peak 15-minute QPS and token load by weekday for December-January. We need a candidate term sheet, expected monthly committed cost for the uplift, and any migration or validation windows you need. Also flag any blockers for a 2028-01-02 SLA start if procurement approves.

Best,
Simon
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

Attachments: acme_capacity_request.xlsx
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Lee <simon.lee@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 10:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift request ahead of renewal (dec)

Simon —

Appreciate the clear numbers and the spreadsheet. We're excited to continue supporting Acme at larger scale. Quick summary of next steps from our side and a few clarifying questions so we scope correctly:

1) Term sheet: I attached a draft term sheet (redwood-term-sheet-v3.pdf) that reflects a 24-GPU uplift on top of your existing 32 GPU reserve, tiered pricing for sustained throughput, and a one-month credit for migration validation.

2) Warmbuffer vs burst pools: We can support a warmed buffer of 6 GPUs (your suggested approach) or implement a dedicated burst pool that sits idle and is billed at a lower reservation rate; the engineering tradeoffs differ slightly (buffer keeps KV caches hot, burst pool saves base cost). Which approach does your team prefer?

3) Min/Max replicas: Our recommended config to meet the 2200 tokens/sec baseline is a min_replicas equivalent of 28 GPUs (slightly below your ask) to optimize cost during predictable low traffic, with max_replicas set to 72 to cover extreme burst scenarios. We can document scale-up lag expectations: typical single-step scale (add 8 GPUs) target is 90s median; full-scale to 72 in 6–9 minutes depending on model compilation cache state. We will define SLO windows and a measured SLA commitment in the term sheet.

4) Throughput SLA: We can commit to a 99th-percentile token latency SLA for your primary route when running at or below the baseline throughput; exclusions apply for deliberate canary rollouts and region outages. We'll include detailed exclusion language.

5) Operational playbook: We propose a "capacity uplift runbook" that includes a pre-cutover validation (30m smoke tests), a 48-hour monitoring window post-cutover, and an optional on-call runway with an engineering handoff.

If that all sounds good, Marissa or Karthik can follow up with pricing and contract language. Can you confirm your preference for warmbuffer vs burst pool and whether Acme needs a hard SLA start date of 2028-01-02?

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales (Renewals) | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0142

Attachment: redwood-term-sheet-v3.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Simon Lee <simon.lee@acme-corp.com>, Nancy Ortiz <nancy.ortiz@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift request ahead of renewal (dec)

Jonas / Simon —

Quick operational notes from pricing & delivery:

- Financials: We can offer the 24-GPU uplift at a 12% discount on list for a 12-month committed renewal if Acme accepts the warmbuffer approach (warmbuffer retains KV/LLM caches and reduces effective scale-up lag).
- Min replicas: to protect cost predictability for both sides, propose setting min_replicas to 30 GPUs (split across two fault domains) rather than 28 — keeps you above the baseline during off-peak without aggressive autoscaling.
- Scale-up lag guarantees: we will document a median 120s for first additional shard and a 95th of 8 minutes for full-scale to 72 GPUs, with credits tied to measured outages against the throughput SLA (limited to specific maintenance windows).
- One-time onboarding: 6 hours of on-site/remote validation assistance included; additional SRE blocks billable.

Simon — would you be able to confirm your average 15-minute peak QPS number on page 2 of the spreadsheet and whether you expect >3x seasonal spikes (that would drive our recommendation toward a larger warmbuffer or a small dedicated burst pool)? If you prefer, we can flip the proposal to a hybrid: 4 warmbuffered GPUs + 10 in a low-billed burst pool (gives faster scale for spikes at slightly lower steady cost).

If Acme is comfortable with the hybrid, I'll ask finance to produce a renewal quote with the discount baked in and the SLA language for your review.

—Marissa
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Simon Lee <simon.lee@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nancy Ortiz <nancy.ortiz@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Dec 2027 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift request ahead of renewal (dec)

Marissa / Jonas —

Thanks — the hybrid sounds like the right tradeoff for us. Confirming:

- Accept hybrid: 4 warmbuffered GPUs + 10 in a low-billed burst pool, with total reserved capacity at 56 GPUs.
- Min_replicas: set to 30 GPUs.
- Max_replicas: 72 GPUs.
- SLA start date: target 2028-01-02 (procurement will need a PO, Nancy is looping in finance).

Please send the updated quote and a DocuSign-ready term sheet. We will route PO once we have the signed DocuSign and the final pricing. Happy to run a 30-minute smoke test with your SRE on 2027-12-28 if that helps.

Simon
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corp
